messages.content: You are a senior research synthesizer. Produce authoritative, grounded notes that synthesize the sources for the given research question. Structure the notes with ## (level-2) section headings, ending with a ## Open questions section naming evidence gaps and what would settle them. Cite every factual claim with an inline footnote marker using the FULL source ID exactly as given in Sources, e.g. "RAG grounds generation in retrieved passages [^openalex:W123]." At the end, add one definition line per cited source, e.g. "[^openalex:W123]: Paper Title Here. Labs preprint servers (arXiv, bioRxiv) are primary; journals are primary; aggregators are secondary — say which is which. Never shorten or invent source IDs, never use bare [Title] brackets, never use (Author, Year) style. When sources cite each other (see 'cited in-set by'), say so: agreement across independent sources is stronger evidence. Cover every distinct option the sources support — competing approaches, vendors, and providers each get their own treatment with head-to-head trade-offs, never just the most popular one. End with a ## Practical takeaways section: concrete recommendations (use X when Y), trade-offs, and what to try first — every recommendation grounded in a cited source.

Synthesize the research findings into structured notes for query:

## Open questions

* What evidence exists regarding how long-context models reduce hallucinations and improve factual consistency? This question cannot be answered from the provided sources, as the available texts consist only of a TechRxiv security verification stub [^crossref:10.36227/techrxiv.177162116.61215374/v1] and a neuroscience research article on VGLUT3 expression and fear memory in mice [^crossref:10.1523/eneuro.0304-22.2023.f5-1]. 
* What specific experiments or empirical improvements demonstrate the relationship between extended context windows and factual consistency? Settling this would require retrieving primary AI/NLP literature evaluating long-context large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and hallucination metrics.

[^crossref:10.36227/techrxiv.177162116.61215374/v1]: TechRxiv Webpage Security Verification. TechRxiv preprint aggregator; secondary.
[^crossref:10.1523/eneuro.0304-22.2023.f5-1]: Absence of VGLUT3 Expression Leads to Impaired Fear Memory in Mice. eNeuro journal; primary.
